messages:
maria_support: Hi team — customer IT (tenant: corp-inc) opened an escalation: after our recent auth-hardening push, some users are getting forced MFA loops. They authenticate via Azure AD SSO, get redirected back, but the app immediately asks for MFA again. Works in Firefox and Safari, breaks in Chrome on managed Windows devices. Ticket: https://support.internal/tkt/86022 :confused:

customer_it: Repro steps we captured:
1) Click 'Sign in' -> Azure AD login and MFA completes.
2) Redirect back to app with code -> our server hits /oauth/token and responds 200 and sets cookie.
3) On redirect complete, client immediately sees login screen and console shows 401 on /session/validate with body: {"error":"session_invalid","detail":"mfa_required"}
4) If we refresh once or open a new tab it sometimes lands successfully. Intermittent and reproducible on Chrome 115+ enterprise.

diego_auth: Thanks. Can you paste the Set-Cookie header from /oauth/token (redacted) and the failing request's Cookie header? Also, are these users behind an iframe widget or using the top-level app?

customer_it: Top-level app first, but they have a launcher that opens an embedded webview for some flows. Set-Cookie: session=REDACTED; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=3600; Domain=.corp-inc.com
Cookie header on failing call: session=REDACTED; __Host-device=XYZ

adele_security: SameSite=Strict stands out. If the redirect back is done via top-level navigation it should be fine, but if any intermediate is happening (like a postMessage or hidden iframe used by their launcher) the browser may treat cookie as third-party and drop it. Chrome's enterprise defaults can be stricter. Also check for recent change we pushed: 'Require Secure+SameSite=Strict for tenant cookies' — we tightened defaults yesterday.

maria_support: The customer insists nothing changed on their side. They say behavior started immediately after our auth-hardening deployment.

diego_auth: Right — our rollback matrix shows the auth-hardening included switching default session cookie SameSite from Lax to Strict for tenants without explicit widget config. That could explain it. Strict will not send cookie on cross-site navigations including some SSO redirect flows that insert intermediate domains. For webviews and some enterprise launchers, the redirect chain can be treated as cross-site.

customer_it: Is there a quick fix? Our users are blocked.
diego_auth: Short-term options:
- Option A: revert to SameSite=Lax for corp-inc only (tenant-scoped rollback) — low risk and quick.
- Option B: implement a top-level cookie bridge: when token exchange completes, return a tiny redirect page hosted on our domain that performs a top-level navigation to set the cookie first-party then navigates back to their app — no customer changes but slightly more intrusive UX.
- Option C: ask customer to change launcher to preserve top-level navigation (will take weeks).

adele_security: Security implications:
- A is straightforward but loosens protection for that tenant.
- B is acceptable if the bridge page only sets a short-lived cookie (<=5m), enforces PKCE/state, and is tenant-scoped behind a feature flag. We must ensure the bridge does not create open redirect or CSRF risks. Logs should not store raw tokens.

sre-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T07:40Z -> auth-hardening roll-out completed. No active rollbacks.

maria_support: Customer wants no client changes. They asked we do something server-side and keep the impact limited to their tenant. Prefer not to revert platform-wide config.

diego_auth: Proposal: tenant-scoped "cookie-bridge" feature. Flow:
1) After /oauth/token, if redirect includes query param bridge=true (we'll set this for tenants enrolled), instead of immediate 302 to app URL, respond with a small HTML page on our domain that sets a short-lived cookie (path=/; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=300) via JS and then forwards to the original app URL. This ensures a first-party cookie set on our domain that the subsequent fetches to api.redwood-inference.com will attach.
2) Bridge page requires PKCE/state validation and only created for known redirect_uri hosts of the tenant.
3) Feature behind per-tenant flag 'cookie_bridge_v1' enabled for corp-inc.

adele_security: I approve under conditions:
- cookie TTL <= 300s and marked HttpOnly if possible
- bridge page must be CSRF hardened and only set cookie for exact tenant domains
- audit logged 
- one-time token handshake built-in so bridge can't be reused

sre-bot: infra note -> may need to increase short-lived session table capacity; queueing infra ticket.

maria_support: ETA and rollout plan?

diego_auth: I can submit a small patch today: server changes to detect tenant flag, generate one-time bridge token (store in redis, TTL=30s), return HTML that performs `fetch('/bridge/consume?token=XXX', {credentials: 'include'})` to set cookie and then `window.location = ORIGINAL_REDIRECT`. Tests + feature flag gating. Expect PR -> review -> canary -> enable for tenant. If infra prioritizes redis, we can do canary within 36hrs.

customer_it: Please prioritize. Our enterprise users are losing productivity.

adele_security: Also add monitoring: per-tenant metric for 'auth_failures_mfa_loop' and alert if >1% after fix. Ensure token values are never logged; store only token hashes if needed.

maria_support: I'll tell the customer: "We're enabling a tenant-scoped compatibility bridge that will be deployed behind a feature flag. No action required on your side. ETA: Friday morning. We'll keep you posted and monitor login success rates." :white_check_mark:

customer_it: Thanks. One more ask: can you include a short explanation for our security team about why this is safe? They audit everything.
diego_auth: I'll prepare a one-page summary covering the constraints (TTL, one-time-use, PKCE/state validation, tenant-scoped, CSRF protections) and share it here for sign-off.

adele_security: I'll review the summary once posted. Also ensure the bridge HTML is small and served over HTTPS with HSTS.

sre-bot: infra ticket created: redis-ephemeral-queue id 8921. Estimated provisioning 3 hours.

maria_support: Closing this thread for now; follow-ups: @diego_auth implement cookie-bridge behind flag, @sre-bot follow infra ticket, @adele_security review summary. I'll update the ticket with progress.

customer_it: Appreciate the quick action, team. We'll verify on Monday when users log in again.
